html:
From August 2017 more than 700,000 Rohingya fled from Myanmar into Bangladesh, settling in camps near Cox's Bazar. With earlier refugees, nearly a million now live there, in what is often called the world's largest refugee camp.

The Rohingya are a mostly Muslim people of Rakhine State in western Myanmar. Myanmar denies most of them citizenship, and they had fled army attacks before, in 1978 and in 1991 and 1992. In August 2017, after attacks on police posts by a Rohingya armed group, the army burned villages and killed thousands. A United Nations inquiry called it genocide, and Gambia brought a case against Myanmar at the International Court of Justice; see Rohingya genocide.

Bangladesh opened its border but wants the refugees to go back, and has moved some to the flood prone island of Bhasan Char. Return has not happened, since conditions in Rakhine remain unsafe. The same flight seen from the Myanmar side is Rohingya exodus.
sum: From August 2017 more than 700,000 Rohingya fled from Myanmar into Bangladesh, settling in camps near Cox's Bazar. With earlier refugees, nearly a million now live there, in what is often called the world's largest refugee camp.
